segments.text: Hello everyone! So, CodeVita
registrations are now open. For those
who don't know me, this is a small gift
from my side. My name is Pratyush
Narayan; I cleared CodeVita myself in
2021, and I have been teaching here for
a year, teaching DSA and more to
thousands of students. I am not here to
tell you about the exam pattern or how
many questions will be asked, as plenty
of random people will tell you that.
You will find a link in the description
to this website; open it, there is no
need to log in, and you don't need to
pay a single rupee. It contains
everything from the exam pattern to
dates, registration, study methods, and
where to study from! What resources to
study? Which videos to watch? Previous
year question papers, mock tests—
treat this as a complete course, not
just a roadmap, because in the coming
month, many people will suddenly launch
their own courses that have nothing to
do with TCS. Don't fall for those 79 or
129 rupee courses. So, first of all,
open the website. Registrations here
will close in eight weeks, on November
15th. We will have you fully prepared
before that. You don't need to study
anything outside of this for TCS
CodeVita. And please, study with full
seriousness because the job market is
already in a bad state. Doing well in
CodeVita will get you a direct
interview. You can land a job worth up
to 13 lakhs through it. So, don't take
it lightly, thinking you'll just sleep,
plan, and study later. No, that time
has passed. You will be ruined. So,
first of all, come here. Let me tell
you about the pattern. A day-wise plan
is written here for you. For Day 1,
your task is to go and register first.
The link is provided there. As soon as
you do that, your registration will be
complete. After that, you can open it
day-wise. It is written exactly what
videos you need to watch and what
questions you need to solve. Where you
need to do them from. Just follow it
every day, and you will be prepared in
56 days. You will also find previous
year questions in it. So, if you feel
you have mastered everything and are
doing really well, you can go to the
previous year question bank, where the
link to every question is provided. Go
read the questions, understand them;
it’s been a long time since I taught
DSA in this playlist. So, I am thinking
that in the upcoming videos of this
playlist, I will solve all these
questions for you, and they aren't very
hard. I mean, it says "hard" in some
places, but they aren't really that
hard. All these questions are just at a
medium level. Okay? So, I will show you
that as well. One very important thing
before we begin: the CodeVita format
has changed a bit. Earlier, six
questions were asked. The exam used to
be six hours long. The current exam
will be three hours long. So, whether
they will ask three questions or six in
those three hours is not confirmed yet.
But this round—the coding round where
you have to build solutions—If you
don't clear this, you won't be able to
move forward. So take this very
seriously; only coding will be asked
here. Previously, eight languages were
allowed. Now, only four languages are
allowed. C, C ++, Java, Python; just
remove C for DSA. So, you can do it in
only three languages. C ++, Java, and
Python. That’s why I’ve been
screaming for a year that DSA should
not be done in JavaScript. So, those
who know these three languages,
that’s great. For those who don't,
those who were doing web development in
JavaScript, Day One has a second task
for you. Pick one language. Choose any
one language, and don’t worry about
where to study it from once you've
chosen. There is a solution for
everything here. You can see the basics
are written there for you. Day One is
optional for you. If you don't know the
basics of these three languages, go
watch the video and learn the basics.
If you know the basics, don't read
anything from here. Do you understand?
Keep solving daily tasks, and you will
be completely prepared; please take
this seriously. When I make the PYQ
video, watch the PYQs very carefully to
see what kind of questions are asked.
How to read them and how to solve them.
Do you understand? So, go check it out
now. If you have anything related to
this, please comment, and I will try to
reply to the comments. Alright, thank
you very much for coming. This is a
very short video. I won't waste much of
your time. Go open your website. There
is no need to log in. Once you open it
in Chrome, your progress will be saved
forever. Keep checking them off as you
go. Right? Alright, see you in the next
video. Thank you so much for coming.
